answer: India's Aadhaar enrolls 1.38 billion residents by scanning fingerprints and irises, then checking each newcomer against the database before issuing a 12-digit number. Anyone who enrolled once is caught the instant a scanner reads their iris again. Forging 10,000 agents means recruiting 10,000 people to give up their biometrics, about $1 each plus travel, and every repeat attempt leaves a trail back to the same body. The river of identities runs dry at the scanner: the signal of a duplicate iris is unmistakable, and no sable ink on a card passes a live check.
